text:
[RCTS.1.2.18] **`replay_refused`: a recording the replayer must refuse.**
A fixture whose `expect.kind` is `replay_refused` carries `steps`, the
session's inputs; `code`, the status the refusal must carry, as the negative
integer in a string; and exactly one of `mutation`, an object; `late_start`,
an integer; and `replay_cache_cap`, an object. A harness must record the
session with the runtime's own recorder, alter the recording as `mutation` or
`late_start` says, and replay it into a fresh engine with the runtime's own
replayer, bounded as `replay_cache_cap` says. The runtime passes only when the
unaltered recording replays with no refusal into a fresh engine with no cache
bound, and the altered one is refused with `code`. A harness must fail a
fixture with more or fewer than one of the three, and a fixture of any other
`expect.kind` that carries `replay_cache_cap`.

`replay_cache_cap` alters the engine the recording is replayed into, not the
recording. It is an object as [RCTS.1.2.25]'s `cache_cap` is, and a harness
must set its bounds on that engine before the load, and on no other. The
recording engine has none, so a `CacheSeed` it recorded can be one the
replaying engine refuses ([RFCS.26.2]).

`late_start: N` alters when the recording begins, not what it holds. A harness
must run the first N `steps` on the writer before its recorder is attached and
record only the steps after them, so the recording begins part-way through the
run and its first event's `seq` is not `0` ([LTIM.2.8.5], [LFST.5.3]). The
unaltered recording is the same session recorded from its first step. A
harness must fail a fixture with a `late_start` that is not an integer from 1 to one less than the number of `steps`, or first N
`steps` that put no event on the stream, after which the recording would
begin at `seq` `0`.

`mutation`'s `op` is one of a closed set, each member tied to the reader clause
the altered recording breaks. Every member but `drop_schema_def`, `drop_fault`
and `append_engine_error` keeps every length in the recording; those three
remove or add whole atoms and change no byte of any other atom:

- `rename_schema`, with `from` and `to`, two schema names of one length in
  UTF-8: every occurrence of `from`'s bytes in the recording is replaced by
  `to`'s, so the recording asserts a schema the program does not hold
  ([RFCS.5.4]);
- `retract_unknown_fact_id`: the `fact_id` of the recording's first
  `FactRetract`, one varint byte, is replaced by `127`, an id no `FactAssert`
  or `FactEmit` in the recording carries ([RFCS.7.3]);
- `merge_timetags`, with `firings`, two integers i < j: the i-th and j-th
  `RuleFireAnnotation`s of the recording, counting from 0 in stream order;
  every occurrence of the j-th's `timetag`, in a `RuleFireAnnotation`,
  `CallIssued`, `ComputationError` or `BoundsError`, is replaced by the i-th's, so two firings the engine keeps
  apart share one `timetag` and the pairing breaks ([LFST.9.3.6]);
- `split_timetag`, with `atom`, an integer from 0: the `timetag` of the
  `atom`-th `CallIssued` of the recording, counting from 0 in stream order,
  is replaced by the least nonzero value of the same varint width that no
  `RuleFireAnnotation`, `CallIssued`, `ComputationError` or `BoundsError` in
  the recording carries, so one firing's atoms carry two recorded
  `timetag`s and its one re-derived `timetag` meets a second recorded one:
  [LFST.9.3.6]'s second direction, which `merge_timetags` does not reach;
- `unknown_capability`: the first entry of the recording's `StreamHeader`
  `capabilities` is replaced by `127`, a number `Capability` does not
  allocate, so the header lists something that is no member ([RBND.1.3]);
- `withdraw_cause`, with `index`, an integer from 0, and `cause`, an
  integer from 1 to 127: the `index`-th `FactWithdraw` of the recording,
  counting from 0 in stream order, has its `cause`, one varint byte,
  replaced by `cause`, so the recorded withdrawal differs from the one the
  replayer re-derives. A reader carries a cause the enum does not hold
  ([RFCS.7a.2]), and the atom is compare class ([RFCS.7a.3]), so the
  refusal is the comparison's, not the decoder's;
- `publish_name`, with `index`, an integer from 0; `field`, `schema_name`
  or `rule_name`; and `to`, a string: that field of the `index`-th
  `FactPublish` of the recording, counting from 0 in stream order, is
  replaced by `to`'s UTF-8 octets, so the recorded publish differs from the
  one the replayer re-derives ([RFCS.27.2]);
- `seed_after_event`: the recording's first `CacheSeed` is moved, its frame
  whole, to just after the first atom that is neither the `StreamHeader`, a
  `SchemaDef`, a `Slot` nor a `CacheSeed`, so a seed follows an event atom,
  which no recorder writes ([RFCS.26.2]);
- `fault_node`, with `atom`, `TypeError` or `ComputationError`: the `node_id`
  of the recording's first such atom, one varint byte, is raised by one, so the
  recorded fault differs from the one the replayer re-derives ([LFST.9.3.1]);
- `drop_fault`, with `atom`, as `fault_node`'s: the recording's first such atom
  is removed, its frame whole, so the replayer re-derives a fault the recording
  lacks ([LFST.9.3.1]);
- `append_engine_error`: an `EngineError` with `fault` 1, `seq` 999 and
  `rule_name` `r` is added after the recording's last atom, so the recording
  holds a fault the replayer does not raise ([RFCS.6.7]);
- `drop_schema_def`, with `schema`, a schema name S: every `SchemaDef` atom
  whose `schema_name` is S, and every `Slot` atom whose `schema_name` is S, is
  removed, and every `FactAssert` naming S is kept, so the recording asserts a
  schema it never announced ([RFCS.5.3], [RFCS.5.4]).

A harness must fail a fixture whose `mutation` names no member of the set, or
has no site in the recording: no `from` to rename, no `FactRetract`, a
`fact_id` wider than one byte, an id `127` the recording carries, an
`ExternalAssert`, whose `fact_ids` the second member does not read, no i-th or
j-th `RuleFireAnnotation`, two that already share a `timetag`, two
`timetag`s whose varints differ in width, no `atom`-th `CallIssued`, one
whose `timetag` is not written, no free value of its width, a `StreamHeader` whose
`capabilities` are not written packed or begin with an entry wider than one
byte, no `index`-th `FactWithdraw`, one whose `cause` is not written (proto3
writes no default) or is wider than one byte, a `cause` equal to the one it
would replace, no `index`-th `FactPublish`, one whose `field` is not written, a
`to` of another length in UTF-8 than the value it would replace or equal to it,
no `CacheSeed`, no such event atom after the first, no
`SchemaDef` for S, no `FactAssert` naming S, no such fault atom, an `atom` of
another name, a `node_id` not written, wider than one byte or of `127`, a
recording that does not walk to its end for the last two members, or one that
already holds an `EngineError` for the last. The set grows only by a
change to this clause.
